reasons: F05, F06: auditor change within two years combined with a disclosed disagreement with accountants is a rare and serious red flag about accounting judgments.
F01, F02, F03: material weakness in internal control (area 'other') with no auditor ICFR attestation, so control failures are unverified by an outside party.
F04, F21, R16: going-concern doubt alongside capital raising and securities issuance creates strong pressure to present favourable results.
F11, F14: material related-party transactions and a CEO/CFO change in the year raise governance and override risk.
R09, R17: Beneish M-score above -1.78 and Dechow F-score above 1.0 both flag likely manipulation.
R04, R02, R15: very high sales growth (>40%) together with sharply falling gross margin and ROA is inconsistent and could mean revenue quality problems.
R19: operating cash flow well below net income (<0.8x) means reported earnings are not backed by cash.
R03, R13, R05: high asset quality index, soft assets above 75% of total and sharply slowing depreciation suggest capitalisation of costs or aggressive asset accounting.
F20: incentive pay tied to revenue or EPS adds motive; mitigants (R01, R18, R07, R08, F07, F16, F17) are modest compared with the red flags.
